summary.headline: Epigral Q2 FY27 revenue rose 28% YoY to INR752 crores, but EBITDA grew only 3% to INR136 crores as chlor-alkali margins were squeezed by energy costs.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 28% YoY to INR752 crores on volume growth and better realisations, while EBITDA rose 3% to INR136 crores and PAT rose 26% to INR64 crores. Management said margins remain under pressure from lagged pass-through of volatile feedstock and energy costs, with the chlor-alkali side hit hardest. H1 FY27 revenue rose 21% to INR1,461 crores and EBITDA margin was 22%. Management kept its H2 outlook positive and said CPVC and epichlorohydrin (ECH) capacity expansions are in trial runs with commissioning expected within a quarter.

financial_highlights.change: +28% YoY vs INR589 crores in Q2 FY26
+3% YoY vs INR132 crores; margin about 18%, similar to Q2 FY26 level stated by management
+25% YoY vs INR131 crores; PAT margin 11%

financial_highlights.metric: Derivatives and specialty share of revenue (Q2 FY27)

segments.name: Chlor-alkali (caustic soda, chlorine)
segments.commentary: Management said the chlor-alkali side was the main source of the sequential EBITDA decline due to higher coal and energy prices. Q2 caustic soda ECU realisation was about INR31,000-32,000/tonne, now about INR32,000-33,000; chlorine averaged roughly zero in Q2 and is currently around zero.

segments.name: CPVC
segments.commentary: Realisations were about INR120-125/kg, moving with PVC raw material prices. Utilisation was about 60-65%. Management expects PVC and CPVC prices to rise further in Q3 and Q4.

segments.name: Epichlorohydrin (ECH)
segments.commentary: Utilisation was about 75-80% in Q2. Capacity is set to double with commissioning expected in Q3 FY27; management expects about 50% captive consumption, with the balance sold in the market.

segments.name: Hydrogen peroxide
segments.commentary: Utilisation was about 95% in Q2. A solar-grade hydrogen peroxide plant is expected to be commissioned in Q4 FY27.

segments.name: Chlorotoluene (OCT/PCT)
segments.commentary: Management expects about INR100 crores of revenue this year, with volumes rising quarter on quarter. Management sized the business at about INR300-350 crores at optimum utilisation, and said it will not enter the benzyl chloride/benzyl alcohol chain.

guidance_outlook: Management expects headwinds to persist into the upcoming quarters but remains positive on H2 FY27, which typically outperforms H1 due to off-season effects.
Caustic soda global prices are expected to rise further in Q3 and Q4 FY27 on European winter energy costs; CPVC and PVC prices are also expected to increase in Q3 and Q4.
CPVC and ECH capacity expansions expected to be commissioned within about one quarter of the call.
Hydrogen peroxide solar-grade plant expected in Q4 FY27.
Epoxy resin plant targeted for commissioning by March 2028, with revenue contribution from FY29. MPP (multi-purpose plant) capex is about INR600 crores.

Management estimates gross block rising from about INR3,000 crores to about INR3,500 crores after CPVC/ECH, and to INR4,100-4,200 crores after MPP and epoxy, supporting revenue of about INR5,000-5,100 crores by FY31. Management also cited INR2,900 crores revenue by FY27 in earlier guidance (as referred to by an analyst).
capex_capacity: CPVC and epichlorohydrin expansions are in final stages with trial runs underway; commissioning expected within about a quarter. Gross block expected to rise by about INR500-600 crores.
Epoxy resin and multi-purpose plant (MPP) pilot plants are ready; customer approval process to begin soon. MPP and epoxy capex about INR600 crores; epoxy targeted by March 2028.
Maintenance capex is about 1.5% of gross block annually.

Renewable power: one solar-wind hybrid project commissioned and a second announced; management targets 30-35% of power demand from solar and wind hybrid within 2-3 years. Epigral's contribution is a 26% equity stake in the SPV and a 20-year commitment, with no substantial capex. Total complex power requirement is about 120-140 MW.
demand_pricing: Management said volume demand is recovering and realisations are firming, but margins are under pressure from lagged pass-through of feedstock costs, West Asia crisis effects, freight and domestic transport costs.

Management argued chlorine prices are now positive and will not return to negative territory, as domestic chlorine derivative demand is growing and chlorine price increases are easier to pass on than caustic soda, which is priced globally.
CPVC demand is growing at about 13% CAGR per year according to management. Management said new capacity may cause temporary oversupply, but it expects demand to absorb supply over 3-4 years.
CPVC contracts: large customers are on quarterly pricing and smaller customers on monthly pricing.
Management said there is no direct impact from El Nino, as the company's products are not primarily agrochemical or pharmaceutical inputs.
Management said ECH demand is growing in India and that there is an export opportunity.

qa_highlights.question: Have caustic soda prices risen enough to offset the 60-70% coal price increase, and is chlorine pricing improving because of cost or demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said caustic soda globally has not moved enough to match energy costs. The energy cost increase has been passed through on chlorine, which is priced domestically and where demand from new derivative plants is rising. Chlorine prices are not expected to return to negative levels.

qa_highlights.question: What were ECU and chlorine realisations in Q2 and currently?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 caustic ECU was about INR31,000-32,000, now about INR32,000-33,000. Chlorine was about zero in Q2 and is currently about zero.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA fall sequentially by INR43 crores, and which products drove it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the chlor-alkali business drove the decline due to higher coal and energy costs. It did not give product-level margins and said the company-level margin is about 22-23%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECH, hydrogen peroxide and caustic soda utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: ECH was about 75-80%, hydrogen peroxide about 95%, and caustic soda about 75% in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: How large can chlorotoluene become, and is the company moving into benzyl chemistry?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about INR100 crores of chlorotoluene revenue this year, sized at INR300-350 crores at optimum utilisation. It said it will focus on OCT/PCT and value-added derivatives, not benzyl chloride or benzyl alcohol.

qa_highlights.question: How is the FY31 revenue target of INR5,000 crores split across products, and is more capex needed beyond INR600 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross block of about INR3,500 crores after CPVC/ECH can generate about INR3,600-3,700 crores of revenue. Adding about INR600 crores for MPP and epoxy takes gross block to INR4,100-4,200 crores, supporting about INR5,000-5,100 crores of revenue by FY31. No product-wise split was given.

qa_highlights.question: Where will the doubled ECH capacity go, and when will it be fully utilised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about 50% of ECH to be consumed captively by the epoxy plant, which is targeted for March 2028, with the rest sold in the market. Ramp-up is expected to be gradual, with epoxy revenue from FY29.

risks_watch: Energy and coal costs keep compressing chlor-alkali margins; the company-level EBITDA margin fell to about 18% in Q2 from 22% for H1.
Chlorine and caustic pricing depend on Q3/Q4 global caustic price moves and domestic chlorine demand.
CPVC new capacity from competitors could pressure prices; management expects absorption over 3-4 years.
CPVC and ECH commissioning is due in about a quarter; watch ramp-up pace and utilisation against the current 60-65% (CPVC) and 75-80% (ECH).
Epoxy and MPP customer qualification timelines; epoxy commissioning is targeted for March 2028.
ROCE is 15% and lags the 18% excluding CWIP, so returns depend on commissioning the new capacity.
Management said the June-quarter chemical environment remains challenging; West Asia conflict and freight costs remain open risks.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term demand and the capacity pipeline, but cautious on near-term margins, which management attributed to energy and raw material costs. Management was evasive on product-level margins and on the FY31 product split, and redirected a retail investor's question about promoter buying.
key_quotes: While we are seeing a positive recovery in volume demand and firming product realization, overall margins remain under pressure.
So I would say it is a new norm in the chlor-alkali industry, new environment will begin where the chlorine is almost like we used to give a chlorine and the chlorine price was negative in the past.
So that much of capex is good enough to fetch a revenue in the range of around INR5,000 crores, INR5,100 crores kind of revenue by FY31.

adds.what: CPVC capacity expansion (gross block +INR500-600 crores with ECH)
Epoxy resin plant and multi-purpose plant (MPP), capex about INR600 crores

growth.why: Management guides to FY31 revenue of INR5,000-5,100 crores and remains positive on H2 FY27, backed by CPVC and ECH trial runs (commissioning within about a quarter), rising caustic and CPVC prices, and CPVC demand growth of about 13% CAGR; margins remain pressured by lagged feedstock pass-through, and no explicit FY27 revenue number was given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin about 18% vs 22% for H1, with chlor-alkali hit by coal and energy costs; management expects caustic and CPVC/PVC prices to rise in Q3-Q4, but feedstock pass-through is lagged, so recovery depends on pricing catching up.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: CPVC and ECH expansions are in trial runs with commissioning within about a quarter (ECH capacity doubling, gross block +INR500-600 crores), and solar-grade hydrogen peroxide plant is due Q4 FY27; epoxy/MPP is under construction for March 2028.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 FY27 revenue grew 21% YoY to INR1,461 crores, CPVC demand is growing about 13% CAGR, and new CPVC/ECH capacity comes online, though CPVC utilisation is only 60-65% and ECH 75-80%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex plans are sustained with epoxy/MPP (about INR600 crores) under construction, and the FY31 revenue target of INR5,000-5,100 crores needs gross block to rise to INR4,100-4,200 crores; CPVC/ECH utilisation at 60-80% limits the case for a fresh plant, so a new announcement is less certain.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management remains positive on H2 FY27, which typically outperforms H1 due to off-season effects, and expects Q3-Q4 caustic, PVC and CPVC prices to rise, but gave no explicit FY27 numerical guidance.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management expects headwinds to persist into the upcoming quarters, the June-quarter environment is challenging, and EBITDA fell by INR43 crores sequentially in Q2 on energy costs, with West Asia and freight costs still open risks.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: ECH capacity doubling is due Q3 FY27, solar-grade hydrogen peroxide plant Q4 FY27, and CPVC expansion within about a quarter; epoxy resin follows by March 2028 with revenue from FY29.

rows.label: Caustic and PVC/CPVC price increases in Q3-Q4
rows.why: Management expects global caustic prices to rise on European energy costs, and CPVC/PVC prices to increase in Q3 and Q4; caustic ECU is already up from INR31,000-32,000 to INR32,000-33,000/tonne.

rows.label: Epoxy and MPP customer qualification
rows.why: Epoxy and MPP pilot plants are ready and customer approval is to begin soon, but epoxy commissioning is not until March 2028 and ECH captive use depends on it.

rows.label: Chlorotoluene scale-up
rows.why: Management expects close to INR100 crores of chlorotoluene revenue this year, with volumes rising quarter on quarter, against an optimum-utilisation size of INR300-350 crores.

tone.note: Management was confident on long-term CPVC demand (about 13% CAGR), the capacity pipeline and H2 pricing, but cautious on near-term margins, which it tied to energy and feedstock costs. Analysts pressed on product-level margins and the FY31 product split, and management was evasive on both.
